result.topic_en: Manipulation of sums of greatest-integer (floor) expressions over t = 1,...,b/2, defining functions φ(2b, b−a) and Φ(2b, a) and deriving an expression for a quantity M, in connection with biquadratic residues.

$\varphi(2b,b-a) = \Sigma\left[\frac{(2t-1)(b-a)}{2b}\right] + \Sigma\left[\frac{(t-1)(b-a)}{b}\right]$
$\varphi \quad = \Sigma\frac{(b+1-2t)(b-a)}{2b} + \Sigma\left[\frac{-at}{b}\right] + \frac12 b\cdot\frac12 b +$
$= \Sigma\frac{(b+1-2t)(b-a)}{2b} - \Sigma\left[\frac{at}{b}\right] + \frac14 bb$

$= \Sigma\left[\frac{(2t-1)a}{2b}\right] - \Sigma\left[\frac{at}{b}\right] + \frac14 bb - \frac14(bb+2b)$
$\frac14(a-1-b)b$
$= \Sigma\frac{(2t-1)a}{2b} - \Sigma\left[\frac{at}{b}\right] - \frac14(a+1-b)b$
$\Phi(2b,a) = \Sigma\frac{(2t-1)a}{2b} + \Sigma\left|\frac{at}{b}\right.$
$M = \frac18(p-1)+\frac12 b-\frac14 ab + 2\Sigma\left[\frac{(2t-1)a}{2b}\right]$
$\Sigma\frac{(2t-1)a}{2b} = \Sigma\frac{ta}{2b} + \Sigma\frac{(\frac12 b+t)a}{2b} - \Sigma\left|\frac{at}{2b}\right]$
$= -\Sigma\frac{ta+b}{2b} + \Sigma\frac{(\frac12 b+t)a}{2b}$
$= -\Sigma\frac{ta+b}{2b} + \Sigma\frac{(b+1-t)a}{2b}$
$= -\Sigma\frac{ta+b}{2b} + \Sigma\frac{(b-t)a}{2b} + \frac12(a-1) - \left[\frac14 a\right]$
$= -2\Sigma\frac{ta+b}{2b} + \frac14 b(a-1) + \frac12(a-1) - \left[\frac14 a\right]$
$M = \frac18(p-1) + \frac12 b - \frac14 ab + \frac12 ab - \frac12 b + a-1 - 2\left[\frac14 a\right]$
$- 4\Sigma\frac{ta+b}{2b}$
$= \frac18(p-1) + \frac14 ab + \frac12(a\mp1) - 4\Sigma\frac{ta+b}{2b}$

methods.what: Definition of φ(2b,b−a) as sum of two floor sums over t = 1..b/2
Reduction of φ to a floor sum in at/b plus polynomial term
Expression of φ via sum of [(2t−1)a/2b] and [at/b]
Formula for M in terms of a floor sum
Transformation of the sum of (2t−1)a/2b by splitting and reflection t→b+1−t
